name: CSL Finance Ltd
tagline: Small, very well-capitalised secured-lending NBFC trading BELOW book (P/B ~0.9x, P/E ~6.3x) with a ~15% ROE and 15-21% AUM growth - but PAT growth decelerated to +3.8% in Q1 FY27, asset quality softened over FY26, the SME-retail engine is weak, and the ValuePickr thread is dormant
business_overview: CSL Finance is an NBFC focused on SME and real-estate/non-real-estate corporate lending, having transitioned into its current NBFC form.
fundamentals_table: ~Rs 551 Cr (price ~Rs 242; book value ~Rs 273, i.e. P/B ~0.89x, P/E ~6.3x)
Rs 1,510 Cr Q1 FY27 (+15% YoY); Rs 1,448 Cr FY26 (+21% YoY)
FY26 Rs 86.11 Cr (+19.4%); Q1 FY27 Rs 22.1 Cr (+3.76% YoY - a sharp deceleration)
GNPA 0.95% Q1 FY27 (1.1% Q4 FY26, up from 0.46% a year earlier); NNPA ~0.81% Q4 FY26; PCR ~123%
CAR ~44%, D/E ~1.06 - under-leveraged; liquidity surplus ~Rs 175 Cr
Wholesale 70 / SME retail 30 (Q1 FY27), shifted from 66/34 in FY25 as SME retail underperformed
fundamentals_narrative: CSL Finance is genuinely cheap: it trades below book (P/B ~0.89x, price Rs 242 vs book value Rs 273) on ~6.3x earnings, with a still-healthy ~15% ROE (6.30% ROA) and 15-21% AUM growth. It is also very conservatively run - CAR ~44%, D/E ~1.06, a ~Rs 175 Cr liquidity surplus - which bounds risk but structurally caps ROE. The concerns from the deep read: PAT growth decelerated hard, from +19.4% in FY26 to just +3.76% in Q1 FY27; asset quality softened over FY26 (GNPA rose from 0.46% to 1.1%, easing to 0.95% in Q1 FY27); the SME-retail segment - the higher-yield growth engine - is contracting in share (31% -> 30%) on industry consolidation and bank/fintech competition, so the book is tilting toward lumpier wholesale (construction/real-estate) finance. Promoter holding is 48.16% with no pledge. There is no active ValuePickr diligence and no independent NBFC asset-quality work (SMA pool, wholesale-exposure concentration) available from this pass.
sentiment_summary: Read most recent 50 of 154 posts (single batch, no escalation). Thread has gone quiet for roughly two years -- the only 2026 post is a new reader asking whether the stock is still being tracked.
community_signal: No trusted-roster users posted in this thread. dhruv_dasani (Aug 2026) noted 'haven't been any discussions over this stock for a couple of years' and asked existing holders what has changed their conviction -- no response yet at time of read, meaning there is no fresh community signal (positive or negative) to draw on beyond the fundamentals.
bull_case: Strong, consistent growth (sales +41.2%, profit +38.9%) with healthy return ratios for an NBFC
Small enough market cap (Rs 506 Cr) that continued growth at this pace could plausibly compound into a 10x outcome over 2-3 years
bear_case: NBFC lending carries inherent credit-cycle risk that isn't visible in trailing growth/ROE numbers alone
ValuePickr community coverage has gone dormant for ~2 years -- no active thesis-testing or scuttlebutt to lean on, so this call rests almost entirely on screener-level fundamentals
verdict_headline: A genuinely cheap (below-book, ~6.3x P/E) small NBFC with a ~15% ROE and 15-21% AUM growth - 10x-in-2-3-years on the four_box valuation=yes exception, but conviction held Low-Medium: PAT growth decelerated to +3.8% in Q1 FY27, asset quality softened over FY26, and there is no active community diligence
verdict_reasoning: four_box scores 2.5 with valuation=yes: CSL trades below book (P/B ~0.89x, P/E ~6.3x) with a ~15% ROE and 15-21% AUM growth, so the re-rating gap is not priced. Per the decision table, valuation=yes is the written exception that permits the 10x-in-2-3-years label at a 2.5 score, with conviction capped at Medium.

Conviction set to Low-Medium (not Medium): PAT growth decelerated from +19.4% in FY26 to +3.76% in Q1 FY27, GNPA rose from 0.46% to 1.1% over FY26 (0.95% in Q1 FY27), the SME-retail growth engine is contracting in share, and the ValuePickr thread has been dormant ~2 years - no independent NBFC asset-quality diligence. The realistic re-rating math is ~2-4x over 2-3 years (fair multiple ~1.8-2.5x book + mid-teens book compounding), so the 10x label is explicitly 'unconfirmed'.

Red-flag check: none. Positive net worth (P/B ~0.89x), no pledged shares, promoter holding 48.16% (a control stake, not a collapse), no auditor issue, no SEBI action. GNPA 0.95-1.1% is low in absolute terms.
No trusted-conviction floor (no roster user in the thread; trusted_floor not active).
Re-check on Q2/Q3 FY27: does PAT growth re-accelerate above ~15%, does GNPA stay around/below ~1%, and does SME-retail share stabilise - plus any fresh community diligence on the wholesale book.

four_box.note: Valuation yes: trades below book (P/B ~0.89x, P/E ~6.3x) with a ~15% ROE and 15-21% AUM growth - the re-rating gap is not priced. TAM yes: small (~Rs 550 Cr mcap) NBFC with AUM headroom. Tailwind weak: generic SME/NBFC lending, and SME retail is actually contracting in share. Moat no: crowded secured-lending market, no franchise edge. Score 2.5 - valuation=yes is the decision-table exception permitting the 10x-in-2-3-years label at capped (Low-Medium) conviction; realistic re-rating math is ~2-4x, so 'unconfirmed'.

annual_report_findings: GNPA rose to 1.1% in Q4 FY26 from 0.46% a year earlier; NNPA 0.81% from 0.34% - management attributes it to lower NPA resolutions in H2 and says new underwriting (last 12 months) shows no material delinquencies.
AUM mix shifted to wholesale 69% / SME retail 31% (from 66/34 in FY25); SME retail underperformed on industry consolidation and competition - the book is tilting to lumpier wholesale finance.
Very well capitalised: CAR ~44%, D/E ~1.06 - the NBFC is under-leveraged, which bounds credit risk but caps ROE at ~15%.
Trades below book: P/B ~0.89x, P/E ~6.3x, book value Rs 273 vs price Rs 242; promoter holding 48.16%, no pledged shares.
3-yr sales CAGR ~30%, profit CAGR ~24% - a steady record, but return ratios (ROCE ~14.5%, ROE ~14.8%) sit just below a 15% bar.
quarterly_trend: Q4 FY26: PAT Rs 19.4 Cr; AUM Rs 1,448 Cr; GNPA 1.1% (up from 0.46% a year earlier).

Q1 FY27 (Jun 2026): standalone PAT Rs 22.1 Cr (+3.76% YoY - a sharp deceleration from FY26's +19%); AUM Rs 1,510 Cr (+15% YoY); GNPA improved to 0.95%, PCR ~123%; disbursals Rs 320 Cr, collections Rs 290 Cr; CAR ~44%; liquidity surplus ~Rs 175 Cr; mix 70:30 wholesale:SME.
Q1 FY27 funding: fresh bank sanction Rs 50 Cr + Rs 60 Cr raised via NCDs.
recent_announcements: Q1 FY27 business update (Jul 2026): AUM +15% to Rs 1,510 Cr, disbursals Rs 320 Cr, GNPA 0.95%.
Rs 60 Cr NCD issue + Rs 50 Cr fresh bank line.
Trading window closed 1 July to Q1 results (routine).
Nothing material on M&A, rating action, promoter change, pledge or litigation this pass.
key_new_facts: PAT growth decelerated hard: FY26 +19.4% -> Q1 FY27 +3.76%.
Asset quality softened over FY26 (GNPA 0.46% -> 1.1%, easing to 0.95% in Q1 FY27) - still low in absolute terms but the trend turned.
The growth engine (SME retail) is the weak segment; the book is tilting to lumpier wholesale (construction/real-estate) finance.
The stock is genuinely cheap - below book (P/B ~0.89x), P/E ~6.3x, CAR ~44% - which is the core of the case.
open_questions: Is the FY26 NPA rise a resolution-timing blip or the start of credit-cycle deterioration in the wholesale book?
Does SME-retail growth recover, or does the book keep tilting to lumpier construction finance?
Why did PAT growth drop to +3.8% - NIM compression, higher provisions, or opex?
With CAR ~44%, will management lever up (lifting ROE) or stay conservative?
deep_dive.conviction_update: Low-Medium -> Low-Medium. The stock is genuinely cheap (below book, ~6.3x P/E) with a still-healthy ~15% ROE and 15-21% AUM growth, which keeps the 10x label alive via the four_box valuation=yes exception. But PAT growth decelerated to +3.8% in Q1 FY27, asset quality softened over FY26, the SME-retail growth engine is weak, and there is no active community diligence - conviction stays Low-Medium, unconfirmed.

chain: NIM x AUM = net interest income

earnings_chain.operating_leverage: unclear - AUM +15% in Q1 FY27 but PAT only +3.8%, so leverage is not currently flowing through
assumed_links: NIM x AUM = net interest income

market_expectation.implied_growth_cagr: at P/B ~0.89x with ~15% ROE the market implies almost no growth or a credit-quality concern; a re-rating to a fair ~1.8-2.5x book for a 15% ROE NBFC plus mid-teens book compounding is the case - a plausible 2-4x over 2-3 years, not a 10x
market_expectation.our_fy28_estimate: AUM ~Rs 2,000-2,200 Cr, PAT Rs 115-135 Cr if SME retail recovers and credit costs stay contained; book value toward Rs 330-360
market_expectation.gap_basis: the market prices CSL below book as if growth has stalled and credit is deteriorating; our path is mid-teens book compounding at a stable ~15% ROE, which a below-book multiple under-rates - though the re-rating math supports ~2-4x, not the 10x label
market_expectation.data_caveat: no broker consensus; implied path is a reverse-P/E estimate + screener.in forward figures + VP thread view

catalyst.event: 2-3 quarters of PAT growth re-accelerating above ~15% with GNPA held around/below ~1% and SME-retail share stabilising

value_chain.position: small, well-capitalised regional NBFC (7 states, ~43 branches); wholesale-tilted book
value_chain.bottleneck_node: underwriting quality in a competitive SME market + wholesale-exposure concentration
value_chain.note: SME lending supply is abundant and competitive (banks, NBFCs, fintechs), which is exactly why CSL's SME-retail growth stalled and the book tilted to lumpier wholesale finance; no structural moat - the edge is conservative capital plus a cheap (below-book) starting valuation.

drivers: wide CAR / low leverage bounding risk (and ROE)
credit costs - GNPA rose over FY26
wholesale-book yield vs a shrinking SME-retail mix
earnings_quality.normalised_note: ROE ~15% at CAR ~44% is a conservatively-geared, mid-cycle return, not a peak; the risk is credit quality in the wholesale book, not a margin that is above trend.

growth_trajectory.last_quarters_note: PAT YoY: FY26 +19.4%, Q1 FY27 +3.76%. AUM YoY: +21% FY26 -> +15% Q1 FY27. Both loan growth and profit growth are decelerating, and the SME-retail segment is contracting in share.
growth_trajectory.reverse_pe_note: P/B ~0.89x already prices deceleration / a credit concern; a 15% ROE deserves ~1.8-2.5x book, so the multiple is low - but the earnings trend must stop decelerating for the re-rating to trigger.

management_quality.capital_allocation: Conservative: CAR ~44%, D/E ~1.06 - carries far more capital than it deploys, which bounds risk but caps ROE at ~15%. Grew AUM 21% in FY26 while letting SME retail shrink rather than chase weak credit. No unrelated diversification.

quality_metrics.open_questions: FCF conversion and net-debt/EBITDA are not meaningful for an NBFC; the relevant lens is asset quality (GNPA trend, SMA/restructured pool, wholesale-exposure concentration), which is only partly visible from this pass - GNPA rose from 0.46% to 1.1% over FY26 before easing to 0.95%.

track_record.note: FY23-FY26 checked for revenue growth >=10% AND ROCE >=15% in the same year. Growth cleared 10% every year (3-yr sales CAGR ~30%), but ROCE/ROE have hovered right around or just below 15% (FY26 ROCE ~14.5% / ROE ~14.8%), so roughly 2 of 4 years clear both. Steady but not a high-return record; the wide CAR structurally caps ROE.
